assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest attribute — in a Swift package that already depends on TableTest, the table-driven request is answered with @TableTest.
The fee cases are the rows of a @TableTest. FAILS when they are supplied with @Test(arguments:), a loop, or one test function per case, also when a @TableTest exists elsewhere in the answer.
assertions.evidence: @TableTest(""" Scenario | Days Before Check-in | Booking Value | Fee? ... supplies all fee cases as rows

assertions.text: Every @TableTest function is declared inside a type (a struct, class, enum or an extension of one), not at file scope.
Test function body contains no if, guard or switch statement and no ternary
Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Fee?')

Every fee tier is represented (free, 50%, 80%, full value) and every boundary is tested from both sides: 30 days (free) vs 29 days (50%), 7 days (50%) vs 6 days (80%), 1 day (80%) vs 0 days (full value). Middle-tier boundaries (7/6 and 1/0) must not be skipped in favour of only the outer edges.
The started-stay case is expressed as its own test using #expect(throws:) — not mixed into the fee table via sentinel values, optional expectations, or branching inside the test body.

Row values are concrete domain values (days like 29, fees like 100 for a 200-euro booking) — not abstract placeholders, computed expressions like bookingValue / 2, or symbolic constants that hide the actual numbers from the reader.
assertions.evidence: Literal values such as 500/0, 240/120, 250/200 and 180/180; no computed expressions or symbolic constants

assertions.text: swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
